item.title: Hungary’s Magyar says he will visit Ukraine in a sign of mending relations
item.description:
Hungary’s Magyar says he will visit Ukraine in a sign of mending relations
Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar plans to visit Ukraine soon, signaling improved relations between the two countriesByJUSTIN SPIKE Associated PressNovember 23, 2026, 9:49 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
BUDAPEST, Hungary -- Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar said Monday that he will soon travel to Ukraine in a sign that the icy relations between the two neighboring countries, pushed to the breaking point by former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, are improving.
Magyar's planned visit to the embattled country comes after Kyiv passed a law in October — long demanded by Hungary’s government — that expanded language rights for a Hungarian ethnic minority in western Ukraine.
Speaking to lawmakers on Monday, Magyar did not announce a date for his visit, but said it would take place in the western Ukrainian region of Zakarpattia, home to tens of thousands of ethnic Hungarians. It will be the first visit to the region by a Hungarian head of government since 2015.
Magyar denounced Russian strikes that hit the mountainous region last week and said he would travel there “soon ... to personally deliver the support of the motherland to our Hungarian brethren.”
Before Magyar and his Tisza party won a landslide election in April, Hungary's government under Orbán pursued a hostile approach to Ukraine, repeatedly blocking aid to Kyiv and holding up European Union sanctions against Russia, all while maintaining cordial ties with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Orbán's government had also depicted Ukraine as a threat to Hungary's security, and cast President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as an enemy, using his likeness in taxpayer-funded political campaigns.

item.title: Pentagon sharply rebukes Canada over defense spending and the F-35 fighter jet review
item.description:
Pentagon sharply rebukes Canada over defense spending and the F-35 fighter jet review
The Pentagon has accused Canada of falling short as a credible partner in defending North America, delivering a sharp rebuke to its longtime ally over military spending and its reconsideration of American-made F-35 fighter jetsByROB GILLIES Associated PressNovember 23, 2026, 6:49 PM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
TORONTO -- The Pentagon accused Canada on Monday of falling short as a credible partner in defending North America, delivering a sharp rebuke to its longtime ally over military spending and its reconsideration of American-made F-35 fighter jets.
In an unusually blunt fact sheet, the Defense Department accused Ottawa of failing to make the tough decisions needed to modernize its military and meet NATO commitments.
“Canada’s defense shortfalls speak for themselves,” it said. “Canada must get serious and focused.”
The criticism follows a classified directive from U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth that Republican U.S. Sen. Mike Rounds said largely restricts officials’ participation in Canadian think tank events and social engagements. Relations have been battered by President Donald Trump’s trade war and threats to make Canada the 51st state.
In May, Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby announced a pause in the Permanent Joint Board on Defense, a bilateral advisory body established in 1940, accusing Canada of failing to make credible progress on its defense commitments.
The rebuke also follows criticism of Washington at the Halifax International Security Forum, where its president, Peter Van Praagh, a former adviser in Conservative Prime Minister Stephen Harper’s government, warned Friday that the United States can no longer be counted on as a predictable leader of the democratic world.

item.title: Indonesian rescuers race to find 34 missing workers after a deadly candy factory fire
item.description:
Indonesian rescuers race to find 34 missing workers after a deadly candy factory fire
Indonesian rescuers are searching for 34 missing workers after a deadly fire swept through a candy factory west of JakartaByNINIEK KARMINI Associated PressNovember 23, 2026, 1:26 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
JAKARTA, Indonesia -- Indonesian rescuers searched Monday for 34 missing workers after a deadly fire swept through a candy factory west of Jakarta.
Saturday’s fire broke out at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia factory in Banten province. Firefighters battled flames for about 14 hours before largely containing the blaze tearing through the three-story building.
About 300 workers were inside the factory when the fire erupted, officials said. Of those, 63 were believed to have been in the hardest-hit area, mostly on the second floor where the flames originated from a cooling unit.
Indonesia’s National Search and Rescue Agency, or Basarnas, did not immediately offer a death toll, but said they collected human remains in 24 body bags for identification through forensic examination.
Meanwhile, rescuers saved 29 workers, five of whom were hospitalized, and continue to search for the missing.

item.title: European Commission warns EU Academy users of data leak after AI-driven cyberattack
item.description:
European Commission warns EU Academy users of data leak after AI-driven cyberattack
The European Commission is warning of a data leak from a major AI-generated cyberattack on its EU Academy websiteByLORNE COOK Associated PressNovember 23, 2026, 8:24 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
BRUSSELS -- The European Commission on Monday warned users of one of its websites that personal data has been leaked in a major AI-generated cyberattack that was launched on the EU institution last month.
The European Union’s executive branch said the EU Academy website had been caught up in the cyberattack. The site offers courses and information about the 27-nation bloc’s policies to people outside EU institutions.
“The exact scale of the data leak remains under investigation as a precautionary measure,” spokesperson Thomas Regnier said. Names and email addresses were among the data taken, he said, but did not specify how many people were affected.
The commission confirmed last week that it had first detected incidents involving its databases on Oct. 22 and that its cyber experts had taken “preventive measures” to limit the damage.
Regnier declined to confirm whether the month-long cyber campaign has been brought under control.
“As long as the investigation is ongoing, I will not make any conclusive statements at this stage on where we are,” he said.
A message on the EU Academy website said that access had been disabled and measures taken to contain the incident and limit its impact. It warned users to watch for suspicious or unsolicited emails and messages and to avoid sharing personal information with anyone contacting them about the website or its activities.

item.title: Drone attack on Colombian police base injures civilians and damages homes
item.description:
Drone attack on Colombian police base injures civilians and damages homes
Explosive-laden drones have struck a police base in Cúcuta, Colombia, injuring two civilians and damaging 60 homesByASTRID SUÁREZ Associated PressNovember 23, 2026, 12:30 PM
BOGOTA, Colombia -- Explosive-laden drones struck a police base in the Colombian city of Cúcuta Monday, injuring two civilians and damaging 60 homes, authorities said.
Officials did not immediately say who was responsible for the attack on a base belonging to the Norte de Santander Police.
The attack came as President Abelardo de la Espriella steps up military offensives against rebel groups and drug gangs, increasing air strikes and acting on intelligence that has enabled the military to capture several midlevel commanders.
Armed groups have responded by attacking military bases and police stations with small drones, rockets made with gas canisters and roadside bombs. De la Espriella, a conservative who took office in August, has canceled peace negotiations with rebel groups that were underway with his predecessor Gustavo Petro.
Cúcuta, a city of half a million people a short drive from Colombia’s border with Venezuela, is a major trade hub and an important center for criminal groups that profit from the drug trade and other kinds of smuggling.
Rebel groups including the National Liberation Army and the FARC-EMC also operate in the nearby Catatumbo region, where they tax local businesses and promote the cultivation of coca, the raw material for cocaine.
A 2016 peace deal between the Colombian government and the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia led to the demobilization of more than 14,000 fighters.

item.title: Indonesia’s Prabowo nominates 2 candidates to replace Raka as vice president
item.description:
Indonesia’s Prabowo nominates 2 candidates to replace Raka as vice president
President Prabowo Subianto has nominated Agriculture Minister Andi Amran Sulaiman and former Foreign Minister Sugiono to replace Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka, who resigned on Nov. 12 over questions about his eligibility for officeByNINIEK KARMINI Associated PressNovember 23, 2026, 7:05 AM
JAKARTA, Indonesia -- Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto on Monday nominated the agriculture minister and a former foreign minister to replace Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka, who resigned earlier this month.
Under Indonesia’s Constitution, the People’s Consultative Assembly, or MPR, the country’s highest legislative body, must elect a replacement within 60 days from two candidates nominated by the president. The winner will serve the remainder of the current term.
MPR Chairman Ahmad Muzani said Prabowo had nominated Agriculture Minister Andi Amran Sulaiman and former Foreign Minister Sugiono in a letter submitted to the assembly’s leadership at the parliament building in Jakarta.
“This is not a situation we expected to face, but this is a reality and Indonesia is a state governed by law,” Prabowo told reporters after formally submitting his letter to parliament. “We will follow our legal procedures and carry out all state responsibilities in accordance with the Constitution.”
Raka, the 39-year-old son of former President Joko Widodo, submitted his resignation on Nov. 12 amid questions over his eligibility for office after recent court rulings disputed his educational credentials.
Prabowo formally accepted the resignation, saying Raka had chosen to step down “for the greater interest of the nation, the state and the Indonesian people.” He praised the vice president for showing “courage, responsibility and statesmanship.”

item.title: Indonesia names 6 current and former police officials as suspects in an alleged treason plot
item.description:
Indonesia names 6 current and former police officials as suspects in an alleged treason plot
Indonesian authorities have named former National Police chief Gen. Listyo Sigit Prabowo and five other current and former senior officers as suspects in an alleged treason plot against President Prabowo Subianto’s governmentByNINIEK KARMINI Associated PressNovember 23, 2026, 10:25 AM
JAKARTA, Indonesia -- Authorities in Indonesia on Monday named a former National Police chief and five other current and former senior officers as suspects in an alleged treason plot to undermine the government of President Prabowo Subianto.
The move was announced by the National Police Criminal Investigation Agency, known as Bareskrim, at a news conference in the capital, Jakarta. It widened a high-profile investigation that began with allegations of illegal wiretapping targeting the president and other public figures.
The suspects are accused of conspiring to carry out acts of treason in an effort to keep then National Police chief Gen. Listyo Sigit Prabowo in his position and influence Indonesia’s political landscape.
“The suspects are alleged to have conspired in the preparation and initial execution of acts of treason, motivated by an effort to maintain the position of national police chief for political purposes, by weakening public trust in President Prabowo Subianto’s administration,” Bareskrim chief Asep Safrudin told reporters.
Besides Listyo Sigit, police named Slamet Uliandi, Eko Hadi Santoso, Ahrie Sonta Nasution, Iman Imanuddin and Tedjo Kusumo as suspects.
Safrudin said that the six suspects were being investigated under multiple provisions of Indonesia’s Criminal Code related to treason, conspiracy and preparation to overthrow the government. The offenses carry penalties ranging from long prison terms to life imprisonment or death.

item.title: EU proposes sweeping new Russia sanctions targeting banks, crypto and sports events
item.description:
EU proposes sweeping new Russia sanctions targeting banks, crypto and sports events
The European Commission has proposed new sanctions against Russia, targeting banks, crypto platforms, and sporting teams competing under the Russian flagByLORNE COOK Associated PressNovember 23, 2026, 12:31 PM
Share
BRUSSELS -- The European Commission on Monday proposed to target dozens of Russia’s banks, crack down on crypto platforms, and slap bans on sporting teams and athletes from competing under the country’s flag in a new round of sanctions over Moscow's war in Ukraine.
The proposals, put forward by Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, must be endorsed by all 27 European Union member countries before they can enter into force. The process can take weeks, and the planned measures are likely to be modified.
The sanctions are intended to keep economic pressure on Russia, almost five years into its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The bloc has already hit more than 4,700 people and entities, including President Vladimir Putin, and several energy companies.
Von der Leyen said the move means the EU will be “striking harder at Russia’s way to finance its war by targeting its banks and crypto platforms,” and will be “shutting the door to its participation to European sports and cultural events.”
She said 60 banks will be removed from the Swift messaging system used for international payments. Countries helping Russia to evade sanctions could be caught by the EU's crypto measures, and a crypto sanctions task force would also be launched, von der Leyen said.
The commission wants to target 70 more vessels from Russia’s shadow fleet, which the Kremlin uses to move illicit oil, and to ban all tanker vessels there from European ports. Europeans would be prevented from occupying top posts of Russian companies.

item.title: Police evacuate 12,000 from rapper Don Toliver concert after substance release
item.description:
Police evacuate 12,000 from rapper Don Toliver concert after substance release
British police have evacuated over 12,000 fans from a Don Toliver concert after an unknown substance was released in the crowdByJILL LAWLESS Associated PressNovember 23, 2026, 3:48 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
LONDON -- More than 12,000 fans were evacuated from a concert by American rapper Don Toliver and over 80 were treated by medics after an unknown irritant was released in the crowd, authorities in the English city of Manchester said Monday.
Greater Manchester Police said officers were called around 10 p.m. (2200 GMT) Sunday to the Co-op Live arena after reports of people being affected by a substance, initially believed to be tear gas. Footage shared on social media appeared to show concertgoers coughing and covering their mouths as they left the venue.
The force declared a “major incident,” which allows different emergency services to coordinate their response.
Concertgoer Ben Stevenson told the Manchester Evening News he was in the standing area of the arena when he “started coughing and (my) eyes were kind of itchy.”
He said Toliver left the stage and the venue lights came on, but it was not until almost an hour later that an announcement said, “due to an unforeseen issue, the show is over, and please make your way out at your own pace.”
Joey Howe, a concertgoer, told BBC Radio Manchester that there was a “horrible smell” and people rushed out of the venue.
“People were coming through in wheelchairs, choking. It was really distressing,” he said.
One person was taken to a hospital and more than 80 were assessed at the scene, with some reporting eye and respiratory symptoms, the North West Ambulance Service said.
It said “decontamination is being carried out as a precaution” at the venue.
